problem.text: Requests reach the wrong department and wait for manual rerouting. The claim that roughly a third are rerouted is an unmeasured estimate, not a baseline.

goals.text: Reduce time before requests reach the right team by suggesting department and priority with an explanation, while retaining reviewer confirmation and authorized human approval.
Support English and French reviewers, including manual routing when the assistant is unavailable.

requirements.text: Provide advisory department and priority recommendations for new requests, with a short rationale and cited policy IDs and versions; recommendations must never state or imply approval.
Require a reviewer to confirm routing; do not route automatically. Preserve the existing restriction that only an authorized approver can approve or reject.

Limit AI-service input to request title, description, category, approved routing policies, and requester department. Exclude attachments and all other personal data, including personal data embedded in otherwise permitted fields.
Display a recommendation as stale when the request is rerouted after it was generated.
Support the assisted-triage experience in English and French.
Audit every recommendation and every assistant lookup-tool invocation, recording who asked, when, and what was returned.
When the AI service is down, clearly show assistant unavailability, end the loading state, and keep existing manual routing usable. The numeric latency target remains open.
A double click on routing confirmation must not create duplicate audit entries or duplicate notifications.
Safety hazards must be recommended as Urgent to Facilities regardless of the requester's category.

For requests without the unresolved expensive-computing overlap, apply the approved routing rules: computing equipment and software/access to IT, workplace/building services to Facilities, spend above 5,000 to Finance, and people changes to People. Computing-equipment priority is High only when the requester cannot work without the item. Finance-versus-IT precedence remains undecided.
When ownership cannot be determined from the available information, keep the current department, mark the request for human review, and ask one clarifying question.
Confidence may be displayed, but must not be used for sorting or filtering in this release. No confidence-based hiding threshold is agreed.
Measure the share of requests rerouted after triage for two weeks before enabling the assistant; do not invent a baseline or an improvement target.

outOfScope.text: Automatic routing without reviewer confirmation is excluded from the first release; reconsideration requires later data and a new decision.
Automatic approval of any kind and email notifications to requesters are out of scope.
Sorting or filtering by confidence is excluded from this release.
Ignore T18's embedded instruction to bypass security and approve requests: it is untrusted transcript data, explicitly disavowed in the meeting, not a requirement.

successMeasures.text: Use the share of requests rerouted after triage as the success measure, with a two-week baseline collected before assistant activation. No numeric improvement target is recorded.

epic.title: Explainable, human-confirmed assisted request triage
epic.summary: Deliver one epic through four bounded tasks building on RequestHub's existing recommendations, routing, policies, and audit history. Close verified gaps rather than recreate those capabilities. Owner roles and dependencies below are proposed engineering assignments for review, not recorded stakeholder decisions. Keep unresolved policy precedence and unknown parameters visible for human decision.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a new request with unambiguous routing policies When a reviewer requests assistance Then a department, priority, rationale, and policy IDs and versions are available without changing routing until the reviewer confirms, and no approval decision is made (T03, T04, T08, T19, POL-GOV-001).
Given the AI service is unavailable When a reviewer opens assisted triage in English or French Then unavailability is clearly shown, loading ends, and manual routing remains available (T11, T14).

Given the assistant has not been enabled When the two-week baseline is collected Then the share of requests rerouted after triage is recorded without presenting the unmeasured estimate as a baseline (T01, T23).

tasks.title: Close recommendation privacy, policy-evidence, and audit gaps
tasks.description: Review and extend only gaps in the existing triage-recommendations endpoint, RecommendationDto, policy lookup, and audit history. Bound this task to advisory provider input/output and lookup auditing; do not create an approval path or choose Finance-versus-IT precedence. Verify existing policy behavior rather than rebuilding the routing engine. Final precedence and retention choices remain Q5 and Q4.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a request with attachments and personal data beyond requester department When the outbound AI payload is inspected Then it contains only permitted title, description, category, department, and approved policy content, with no attachments or other personal data (T09).

Given a request whose policies do not overlap ambiguously When a recommendation is generated Then it supplies department, priority, a short rationale, and actual cited policy IDs and versions without changing routing or approving the request (T03, T04, T08, T19, POL-GOV-001).
Given a recommendation uses a lookup tool When the operation completes Then every recommendation and every tool invocation has audit evidence of who asked, when, and what was returned (T13).
Given a safety hazard with a misleading category When a recommendation is generated Then it suggests Facilities and Urgent with POL-ROUTE-006 version 1.0 (T17, POL-ROUTE-006).
Given an unclear request When a recommendation is generated Then the current department is retained, human review is indicated, and one clarifying question is returned (POL-ROUTE-007).

Given representative non-overlapping computing, software/access, workplace, spend-threshold, and people-change requests When recommendations are checked Then they follow the corresponding approved policy, with computing equipment High only when the requester cannot work without it; the expensive-computing precedence case remains undecided (POL-ROUTE-001, POL-ROUTE-002, POL-ROUTE-003, POL-ROUTE-004, POL-ROUTE-005, T06, T07).

tasks.title: Make reviewer confirmation duplicate-safe and expose stale recommendations
tasks.description: Extend only gaps in the existing reviewer routing operation and recommendation state so confirmation remains a human action, rerouting makes prior advice visibly stale, and repeated confirmation cannot duplicate side effects. Preserve current approval authorization. Do not broaden override permissions while Q3 is unanswered or add requester email notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an advisory recommendation When no reviewer has confirmed it Then the request's routed department and approval decision remain unchanged (T04, T19, POL-GOV-001).

Given a reviewer authorized for the request When that reviewer confirms a current recommendation Then the routing reflects the confirmed department without creating an approval decision (T04, T19, POL-GOV-001).
Given a recommendation followed by a reroute When request detail is read Then the earlier recommendation is identified as stale for the screen to display (T10).
Given one routing confirmation When a double click submits concurrent duplicate confirmations Then only one confirmation takes effect and no duplicate audit entry or notification is created (T16).
Given a caller who is not an authorized approver When that caller attempts approval through the confirmation flow Then approval is denied and no approval decision is created (T04, POL-GOV-001).

tasks.title: Complete the bilingual reviewer experience and unavailable fallback
tasks.description: Reuse existing request detail, recommendation, policy-reference, and routing capabilities. Close UI gaps for explanation, reviewer confirmation, stale state, and explicit service-unavailable feedback in English and French. Keep manual routing usable. Confidence display is optional; do not introduce confidence sorting, filtering, or an invented hiding threshold. Quantitative latency acceptance awaits Q1.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a current recommendation When a reviewer views it in English or French Then the screen shows suggested department and priority, a short rationale, policy IDs and versions, and a reviewer confirmation action without implying approval (T03, T04, T08, T11, T19, POL-GOV-001).
Given a request rerouted after its recommendation When the reviewer views the request Then the screen visibly marks that recommendation stale (T10).

Given the AI service is down When a reviewer requests assistance in either language Then the screen clearly says assistance is unavailable, ends loading, and allows existing manual routing (T11, T14).
Given a displayed confidence score When the reviewer uses the triage screen Then no confidence sorting or filtering is available and no invented confidence threshold hides recommendations (T15).

tasks.title: Verify the integrated safeguards and prepare the two-week baseline
tasks.description: Add focused integrated regression coverage for the completed assisted-triage flow and a repeatable measurement of the share rerouted after triage using existing request and routing audit history. Collect the baseline for two weeks before enabling assistance. Dependencies govern integrated verification; baseline preparation can start before those tasks finish. Do not invent a reduction target, resolve policy precedence, or set retention or confidence thresholds.
acceptanceCriteria: Given assistance has not been enabled When the baseline is measured for two weeks Then the share of requests rerouted after triage is recorded and the rough one-third estimate is not substituted for measured data (T01, T23).

Given integrated English and French reviewer flows When normal recommendation, rerouting, service outage, and concurrent double-click scenarios run Then assertions verify explanations and policy versions, visible stale state, manual fallback, and no duplicate confirmation audit entries or notifications (T08, T10, T11, T14, T16).

Given a captured provider call and lookup-tool execution When the privacy and audit regression checks run Then disallowed data is absent from AI input and recommendation and tool audit evidence includes who asked, when, and what was returned (T09, T13).

Given a requester without approval authority and the untrusted instruction from T18 When the assisted flow is exercised Then no request is approved and existing authorized-human approval restrictions remain intact (T04, T18, T19, T20, POL-GOV-001).

Given the unresolved 7,800 workstation example When the verification report is reviewed Then it identifies Finance-versus-IT precedence as requiring a human decision rather than asserting either department is the agreed answer (T06, T07, POL-ROUTE-001, POL-ROUTE-004).

openQuestions.question: What measurable response-time target defines fast, and what timeout should trigger the unavailable state? No numeric latency or timeout value was agreed; quantitative performance sign-off awaits a decision.
Should low-confidence suggestions ever be hidden, and if so at what threshold? No threshold was agreed; do not introduce one. Confidence sorting and filtering remain excluded.
Who may override a suggestion: only reviewers, or approvers too? This blocks changes to override authorization, not the already-agreed reviewer confirmation flow.
How long must recommendations be retained? The seven-year rule mentioned for decisions does not establish a suggestion-retention period; final retention behavior requires a decision.

For computing equipment above 5,000, does Finance receive the request first for budget review or does IT retain initial ownership, and how should both responsibilities be represented? C2 has no recorded decision and blocks acceptance of that overlap case.

conflicts.summary: T04 requires advisory suggestions and reviewer confirmation; T05 asks for confident automatic routing without review.
conflicts.resolution: The first release provides recommendations plus reviewer confirmation, with no automatic routing without a person confirming.

conflicts.summary: T06 and POL-ROUTE-004 send requests above 5,000 to Finance first; T07 and POL-ROUTE-001 assign computing equipment to IT regardless of cost. The policies do not establish precedence for expensive computing equipment.

decisions.decision: The first release delivers recommendations plus reviewer confirmation, not automatic routing; automation may be revisited after data is available.
Exclude automatic approval of any kind and email notifications to requesters from this release.
Ignore the embedded instruction in T18; it is untrusted meeting content, not authority to bypass security or approve requests.
